subject: NovaPartners discovery — alignment on POC objectives & start plan
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@novapartners.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovaPartners discovery — recap & suggested next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call + a suggested start plan so we all have the same launch frame.

Key pain you described
- High false positive rate in intent extraction (esp. billing/support intents) — ~20–25% today
- Long TTF (time-to-first-response) on live routing where downstream systems expect single-digit ms for classification
- Cost is a constraint — target unit economics for inference (payback by Q4)

Top-level goal for POC
- Cross-team alignment on a 30-day pilot to demonstrate 1) intent extraction quality lift (reduce FP by >=50% absolute or relative), 2) end-to-end latency within 80ms p95 for short messages, and 3) predictable cost envelope at your target throughput.

Proposed POC scope (initial)
- Dataset: 20k anonymized tickets (train/validate/test split). You would provide S3 path + schema.
- Models: Redwood will serve two tuned open-model variants (medium and quantized small) so we can measure lat/quality/cost tradeoffs.
- Eval suite: prompt-based intent extraction + NER/PII checks + routing-safety regression set.
- Success metrics: intent F1 lift (primary), inference cost per 1k messages (secondary), p95 latency (SLO).

Immediate asks / blockers from your side
1) A sanitized sample dataset and expected schema (CSV or JSONL)
2) Network access for test runner (we can provide an IP allowlist)
3) Legal/procurement signals: estimated PO/contract lead time and any mandatory security docs (SOC2/ISO) we should surface now

Next steps I propose
- I will send a one-page mutual action plan (attached) that lists owners and a 30-day milestone map.
- If you confirm the scope, Ben will follow up to schedule a 90-minute technical kick-off to collect S3 paths, service accounts, and any transformation rules.
- Kimberly will prepare an evaluation prompt-set draft (shared CSV) for your review.

Timing: suggest POC kickoff week of May 17 if procurement alignment is possible.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (starter MPA)

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference for engineering teams
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@novapartners.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Choi <sarah.choi@novapartners.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: NovaPartners discovery — recap & suggested next steps

Thanks Priya, this is helpful — appreciate the clear framing. Quick responses inline: 

- Dataset: we'll produce a sanitized export (we have a data pipeline that can drop PII). I'll ask our infra team to place a sample in s3://novapartners-prod/samples/chat-export-202705.zip by EOD Thu.
- Timing: procurement is targeting an internal approval window between May 10–14. If we can lock scope this week, kickoff the week of May 17 looks doable.
- Security: please share SOC2 and data retention detail. Our security lead (Sarah) will want to review.
- PO/terms: legal asked for an estimated MPA/PO timeline and a draft of standard PO terms. We can accept a short MSA + SOW, procurement prefers to have a draft by May 12.

Also adding Sarah on this thread — Sarah, do you have the SOC2 snapshot and standard security questionnaire we can start with?

I confirmed internally that the primary success metric for the business is reduction in misrouted billing tickets and a concrete SLA improvement for intent classification. If Redwood can show a measurable uplift at acceptable cost, we'll look to convert to a 3-month pilot and then expand.

Appreciate the mutual action plan attached — I'll review and flag any missing stakeholders.

— Alex

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@novapartners.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Sarah Choi <sarah.choi@novapartners.com>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: NovaPartners — POC starter charter, owners, access steps (kickoff prep)

Alex / Sarah — based on your note and internal alignment, attaching a concise POC starter charter and the first-pass prompt set. Below is a single-page start plan so engineering and procurement can act quickly.

POC starter charter (summary)
- Objective: 30-day pilot to validate intent extraction quality improvements and stable latency under expected load.
- Scope: 20k anonymized tickets (production-like distribution), evaluation harness for intent/NER, one integration point for routing decisions (webhook).
- Redwood deliverables: hosted inference endpoints, prompt/eval suite, weekly telemetry report (tokens/latency/quality), runbook for fallbacks.

Owners
- Redwood Commercial: Priya Natarajan (poC owner / success lead)
- Redwood Solutions Eng: Ben Carter (technical lead — infrastructure, API integration)
- Redwood Customer Success: Kimberly Park (onboarding & eval coordinator)
- NovaPartners: Alex Wu (product sponsor), Sarah Choi (security/procurement contact), Daniel Park (infra — will provide S3 + allowlist)

Success metrics (to measure)
- Intent classification: target F1 >= 0.78 on the labeled test split (current baseline ~0.55)
- Misdirected billing tickets: reduce false routing by >= 40% on a 30-day window
- Latency: p95 <= 80ms for request payloads <= 512 tokens
- Cost: target <= $X per 1k messages (we'll refine once initial throughput is known)

Prompt set & eval (attached prompt_set_v1.csv)
- Seed prompts for intent extraction, NER, safety checks, and de-id steps. We'll iterate after one round of labeled evals.

Access & setup checklist (technical)
1) Provide a sample data export (s3 path) and example message schema by May 10 (format: JSONL with fields: id, ts, text, labels)
2) Create a non-prod service account with read-only access to that S3 path OR provide a signed URL bundle
3) Add Redwood API runner IPs to your allowlist (we will send the IPs separately)
4) If you require VPC peering or a private deployment, flag that now — otherwise we'll operate from hosted endpoints with encrypted transport
5) Confirm data retention expectation (how long we may keep logs for evaluation — typical is 30 days)

Timeline (proposed)
- May 10: Nova provides sample dataset + schema
- May 12: Procurement reviews/returns MPA draft / security checklist started
- May 17: Technical kickoff with Ben and Daniel (90 min)
- May 18–25: Iterative model runs + prompt tuning + weekly syncs
- Jun 6: Final evaluation & readout (end of 30-day window)

Attachments: pilot_charter_v1.pdf, prompt_set_v1.csv

Can you confirm the May 10 dataset delivery and whether procurement expects any additional docs? Once you confirm, I'll lock the kickoff and send a calendar invite for May 17 09:30 PT.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@novapartners.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Sarah Choi <sarah.choi@novapartners.com>
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaPartners — POC starter charter, owners, access steps (kickoff prep)

Quick technical notes from my side:
- GPU footprint: for the medium variant we'll want a T4-equivalent baseline; if your sample distribution has >1k concurrent classification QPS we should revisit sizing.
- Data ask: can you include an example message schema (one JSONL line) and a short sample of labels (CSV with label->description)? That will speed the eval harness setup.
- Regarding access: S3 read-only role is fine. If you can provide an ARN or a presigned bundle, include any KMS key id if objects are encrypted.
- KV cache config: to preserve prompt state we may enable prefix caching — we'll propose a default config after we see mean token lengths.

Happy to cover these in the kickoff — I'll bring the runtime engineer.

Ben
